consensus_summary: No settled consensus exists. Common associations are sunset (endings/decline/darkness/death), the east-west merism for totality or infinite separation (esp. Ps 103:12), Hebrew yam/sea as geographic west (sometimes Gentiles), and minority typological westward approach to God's presence in the sanctuary; liturgical west-facing renunciation of Satan is also noted.
book_summary: West is where a course ends—behind, the destination. Hebrew yam (‘sea’) denotes west; Scripture’s east-facing orientation makes the western sea the ‘hinder sea.’ The after/back/end word-family therefore marks what is last, latter, or westernmost; east and west together span complete separation. Opposite of East.
consensus_core_identification: Unsettled plurality: sunset-endings/death, merism-separation/totality, sea/Gentiles, or sanctuary approach (no single core).
book_core_identification: Hinder/back/end side (where a course ends; the destination/last/latter/westernmost), derived from yam as hinder sea plus the after/back/end word-family; plus east-west complete separation.
boundary_disagreement: No shared baseline; book’s hinder/end word-family and ‘destination/behind’ framing are absent from consensus categories, so boundary comparison does not arise.
material_contradiction: None; book’s claims are compatible with scattered consensus elements (sea, separation, endings) but do not adopt or deny them as core.
rationale: Consensus explicitly marks the symbol as unsettled and lists sunset-endings, merism-separation, yam-sea/Gentiles, and sanctuary-west as the recognized options. The book’s minimum core—west as the hinder/back/end (‘where a course ends—behind, the destination’) via the yam/hinder-sea idiom and after/back/end word-family—is not among those options or their stated extensions. Related fragments (sea, separation, completion) appear, yet the central linguistic-spatial identification and its ‘destination/behind’ gloss do not; hence novelty rather than match, refinement, or contradiction.
strongest_objection: The consensus ‘endings/completion’ (sunset) and ‘sea’ alternatives could be stretched to cover ‘where a course ends’ and yam, collapsing the entry into a refinement rather than a novel core.
